fight_by_fight.fight: Camila Reynoso vs Aieza Ramos Bertolso

fight_by_fight.method_forecast: George Staines by KO/TKO (raw; rejected by route gate)

lessons: Bertolso exposed a winner-model blind spot for elite amateur pedigree and high-level pre-UFC championship experience; capture this prospectively rather than treating a short pro record as low information.
DWCS-M-v0.3 remained too decision-heavy on the completed slate. Reynoso DEC and Diop DEC both missed while all four completed fights ended inside the distance.

Escuza-Borando showed that opponent-specific submission vulnerability should not overpower a fighter's own repeated ultra-early KO/TKO finishing pattern. Early-finish route evidence needs stronger interaction with method selection.
Diop-Sabanov strongly supports round-dependent cardio/freshness and failed-exchange cost features. Diop was fresher in Round 2 and finished Sabanov after a high-output first round.

Staines showed the career-route plausibility gate can be too rigid: a fighter with few historical KO/TKO wins can still have a high TKO path through wrestling, slams or ground damage. Distinguish striking KO history from grappling-generated TKO access.
DWCS-D/R v0.3 regressed sharply from Week 7: 9-15 across all binary duration markets and 1-3 exact round. Keep both shadow-only and do not promote based on Week 7's 12-3 totals result.

Three of four completed bouts ended in Round 1 and all four ended inside the distance. Do not globally inflate early-finish priors from one card, but investigate whether pair-level combined finish pressure and minimum durability are underweighted.
Boosting challenger and production winner both finished 3-1 but made complementary errors. Track prospective Brier/log-loss for both before considering any ensemble or promotion change.
Bulaid-Visconde must remain ungraded and excluded from Week 8 retraining. Re-run the matchup fresh for Week 10 rather than reusing the Week 8 probability lock.
